methodological_rigor.justification: Randomized, open-label, parallel-group phase II trial (NCT05009069) with 3+3 safety run-in and 1:1 randomization of 55 patients post-nCRT to Atezo+Tira vs Atezo monotherapy across five Chinese centers. Standard pCR endpoint with MRI, RECIST v1.1 and AJCC 8th edition tumor regression grading. Key methodological limits: comparisons are made against a 15% historical control rather than a concurrent control; no formal head-to-head comparison between arms; sample size powered at 0.10 two-sided alpha for a large 20% effect; pathology is locally read without central review; and PD-L1/TIGIT/PVR biomarker analyses are exploratory with small numbers. Design is internally consistent and appropriate for a signal-finding phase II but not definitive.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual RCT (Oxford 1b) addressing a clinically important question: whether adding dual checkpoint blockade (anti-PD-L1 + anti-TIGIT) after long-course nCRT improves pCR in pMMR/MSS LARC where ICIs historically have limited efficacy. The Atezo+Tira arm achieved pCR 35.7% vs 15% historical (P=.002), with acceptable grade 3-4 TRAE (31%), suggesting a promising neoadjuvant strategy. Direct clinical applicability is real but preliminary; longer follow-up and phase III confirmation are needed before practice change.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT is applicable and a CONSORT diagram (Fig 1) is included. The paper documents ITT/mITT/safety populations, protocol deviations (one patient crossover), Clopper-Pearson CIs, Kaplan-Meier for time-to-event, and adverse-event grading per CTCAE v5.0. Biomarker assays (SP263, SP410, CD155 D8A5G) and thresholds are specified. However, the primary-endpoint P-value uses a one-sample binomial vs historical control (not a between-arm comparison), which CONSORT expects to be made explicit; patient-level data and code are not shared in the excerpt.

novelty_literature.justification: First reported randomized phase II evaluating TIGIT plus PD-L1 blockade combined with nCRT in LARC, in a pMMR/MSS population where ICI benefit has been limited. Extends prior R-IMMUNE/VOLTAGE-A/UNION work (anti-PD-1/PD-L1 with nCRT) by adding an anti-TIGIT arm and providing comparative activity/safety data. Meaningful novel question and combination but not a first-in-class mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: Structured clearly (IMRAD) with a CONSORT diagram, Kaplan-Meier plot and well-organized tables for baseline, outcomes, surgery and AEs. Methods/Results are precise on doses, schedules and biomarker scoring. Discussion appropriately contextualizes results against RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23 TNT regimens and other ICI-nCRT studies. Limitations section is concise and specific.

key_strengths: First randomized phase II evaluating anti-TIGIT (tiragolumab) plus anti-PD-L1 (atezolizumab) after nCRT in pMMR/MSS LARC
Primary endpoint met in Atezo+Tira arm with pCR 35.7% vs 15% historical control (P=.002) and 100% R0 resection
Acceptable safety with grade 3-4 TRAEs at 31% and no treatment-emergent deaths
Integrated biomarker assessments (PD-L1, TIGIT, PVR) with pre-specified staining platforms and thresholds
Signals a favorable safety profile compared with intensive TNT regimens (RAPIDO/PRODIGE-23 ~45-48% grade >=3 AEs)
key_concerns: Comparison to 15% historical control rather than a concurrent standard-of-care arm; between-arm tests not performed
Small sample size (n=55 randomized) and alpha=0.10 two-sided; biomarker subgroup analyses underpowered
Pathology reviewed locally without central adjudication; short median follow-up (21.55 months) limits survival inference
Open-label design and single-country (China) multi-center setting raise generalizability concerns
No data/code sharing statement; one protocol deviation (crossover) handled post-hoc
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed signal-finding phase II with a genuinely novel combination in pMMR/MSS LARC; appropriate for a solid specialty oncology journal (Tier 2) with minor revisions clarifying the historical-control comparison and adding long-term follow-up commitments.
